capabilities: conduct two-sided chat conversations stored as Markdown files
link vault notes inside messages with [[ wikilinks and autocomplete
attach pictures and files to individual messages
customize participant names, bios, avatars, and chat backgrounds
export plain-text transcripts or view raw Markdown
disambiguation: Not an AI chatbot; both sides of the conversation are written by the user and no AI or network calls are involved.
extras: The README states the project is independent and not affiliated with or endorsed by Alex Hormozi, and explicitly disclaims that it is medical, mental health, religious, or therapeutic advice. No account, analytics, AI API, or network transmission is used.
intentEvidence: Alex Hormozi's public description of his Solomon Project practice inspired the interface.
motivation: The author wanted an easy way to do the letter-writing exercise his pastor suggested, and was inspired by Alex Hormozi's weekly written conversation with his 85-year-old self in a Google Doc.
problem: Self-distanced journaling, like writing letters to and from a wiser persona, has no purpose-built interface in Obsidian and is usually done in a plain document.

relations.evidence: Alex Hormozi's public description of his Solomon Project practice inspired the interface.

summary: Chat-style journaling plugin that turns a Markdown note into a two-sided conversation with a wiser version of yourself for self-distanced reflection.
